title: He didn’t steal the position.
paragraphs:
He didn’t steal the position.
God removed the man who abused it.
Because sometimes… what we call “delay” is actually God clearing out pride before installing purpose.

Eliakim didn’t rise in a moment.
He was revealed in a moment.
And here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

Shebna was already in the room.
Already in power.
Already trusted.
In Isaiah 22, God exposes him—not for lack of talent, but for misused authority. He was building a monument to himself while holding a position meant to serve others.

You can be gifted…
Visible…
Even “blessed”…

What are you building right now…
that has your name on it more than God’s?
Where have you been quietly using what God gave you… for yourself?

That silent compromise.
That delayed obedience.
That subtle need to be seen.
“I will thrust you from your office…” (Isaiah 22:19)
Because God doesn’t negotiate with pride—He replaces it.
“I will clothe him with your robe… commit your authority into his hand.” (Isaiah 22:21)

God is not looking for better talent.
He is looking for surrendered hearts.

Eliakim didn’t campaign for the robe—
he was chosen for the weight.

And when God gives weight…
He also gives keys.
“I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David…” (Isaiah 22:22)
But here’s what most people miss—
That “key of David” doesn’t end with Eliakim.

In Revelation 3:7, Jesus says,
“I hold the key of David—what I open no one can shut, and what I shut no one can open.”
So now the story turns… and it turns on you.
Because this is no longer about a palace in ancient Jerusalem.

You don’t lose calling overnight.
You drift from it quietly—through small, tolerated pride.
We’re still holding positions God has already written Ichabod over.
That’s the part nobody says out loud.
But here’s where grace walks in.
Because the Gospel is not God replacing you.
You and I are not just Eliakim.

We’ve taken what God gave…
and made it about us.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23).
But God didn’t just remove sinners.
The One who didn’t grasp authority—but laid down His life.
Philippians 2 says He humbled Himself… even to the point of death on a cross.

So that prideful people like us…
could be forgiven.

Not by performance—
but by grace.
If you repent—truly turn—He doesn’t just clean you.
Here’s the conviction you can’t dodge:

Some people want Eliakim’s promotion
without crucifying Shebna’s pride.
Not to rebuild your own name—

You are not the architect of your life.
You are a steward of God’s calling.

You are not replaced.
You are redeemed.

What needs to die in you…
so God can trust you with more?

Not out of fear—
but because grace is still reaching.
Jesus is still holding the key.
Not noise. Real discipleship. Stay close to that kind of fire.
If this pierced you, don’t ignore it.
And next… we’re going deeper into the danger of “looking faithful” while slowly losing fire.
